bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Small Business Administration relating to "Citizenship and Residency Requirements and Recission of Procedural Notice 5000-872050" and "Revised Applicant Ownership, Citizenship, and Residency Requirements for 7(a) and 504 Loans".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution would block two Small Business Administration rules that changed citizenship and residency requirements for certain SBA loan programs (7(a) and 504 loans). Under the Congressional Review Act, if this resolution passes both chambers and is signed, the rules would be nullified and the SBA would be barred from issuing substantially similar rules without new statutory authority. The resolution does not specify what the underlying rule changes were or how they altered eligibility.

industries.rationale: SBA 7(a) and 504 loans are administered through participating lenders, so changes to eligibility requirements directly affect the volume and risk profile of these loan programs.
SBA 504 loans are specifically designed to finance commercial real estate and equipment purchases, so eligibility changes affect this sector's access to financing.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.
Banking & Finance is also the top donor sector for 6 other members from NY. That points to the industry being big in the state, not to anything about this member.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
